header.business: Example Candle Co., an online candle and home fragrance store (invented example)
header.attribution: Floor: GA4 last click (session source) plus code-only sales, the orders with a network's own code that GA4 credited to another source or never saw; ceiling: the floor plus the assist uplift from GA4's first user source
header.sources: GA4, Shopify, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, Instagram, Facebook Pages, TikTok and YouTube Analytics, connected through the InsightfulPipe MCP; costs, codes and survey answers from the user

headline: Organic social returned $9,305 to $14,299 of gross profit on $15,597 of cost over 90 days: ROI -40.3% at the floor, -8.3% with assists. Instagram carries it; TikTok can't be judged until it is tagged.

roi_table.why: ROI floor -60.3% with tag coverage 7.1%; sales outside tracking: code-only revenue $2,249 is at least half of tracked $2,002; survey share 22.2% is 4.3x its first-user revenue share 5.2%.
ROI ceiling -30.4% below 0; media value $3,469 is at least the $1,239 cost.
ROI ceiling -57.2% below 0; media value not priced.

totals.media_value: 23165.54 for the three priced networks (YouTube not priced)

key_findings: Instagram pays for its time before any assist is counted: $8,876 tracked revenue plus $1,007 from GLOWIG15 orders GA4 filed elsewhere, against $5,210 of cost, so the ROI floor is 10.0% and the ceiling 43.2%. It earns $53 of floor return per team hour, the most of the four.

TikTok reads as a loss at the floor (-60.3%), even with its code-only sales, but it is barely visible: only 7.1% of its 4,100 sessions were tagged, WICKTOK sold $2,249 outside GA4's TikTok credit against $2,002 inside it, and buyers named TikTok in 22.2% of survey answers while GA4's first-user view gives it 5.2% of store revenue. With assists the ceiling is -24.0%.

Facebook loses money in every view (-37.1% floor, -30.4% ceiling), but its 415,502 organic views would have cost $3,469 at the brand's own Facebook CPM, more than its $1,239 cost. Worth keeping only if reach is a goal.

YouTube returns $328 at the floor and $1,255 at the ceiling on $2,934 of cost (-88.8% to -57.2%), and with no YouTube ads its reach can't be priced. Its tag coverage is low too (8.2%), but nothing points to hidden sales: no code, and 1.8% of survey answers against a 1.9% first-user revenue share.

per_network.reading: above 100%: story links, shared posts and DMs also send visits, so no capture gap shows

paid_rows_excluded.why: paid_social and paid mediums in the Paid Social channel; they belong in a paid report

tracking_check.youtube_channel_note: YouTube referrals sit in GA4's Organic Video channel and are counted as organic.

code_orders.note: no YouTube code, so nothing to add

cost_basis: 40 USD loaded hourly rate; shared tools 119 USD a month split by share of the 92 monthly hours; monthly figures times 90 / 30.

media_value.views_from: lifetime view_count of the 24 videos posted in the window

media_value.own_cpm: no ad spend, no CPM given

media_value_note: Shown beside the ROI, never added to it. The audience_network row of the Meta report is not a network the brand posts on, so it is not used.

where_to_put_effort.move: Move up to 11 hours a month from YouTube to Instagram, and keep 3 hours a month on YouTube to keep the profile alive (the user's own minimum). At Instagram's $53 floor return per hour, that would be about $1,752 more floor return over 90 days. Estimate: it assumes the return per hour holds at more hours, which it may not.
where_to_put_effort.keep: Facebook stays at its current 10 hours a month: its reach covers its cost, so don't add hours until a sale shows up in the floor.
where_to_put_effort.tiktok: TikTok keeps its 32 hours for the next 30 days while tracking is fixed; read it again before moving any hours.

survey_check.note: 490 answers. The survey asks where buyers first heard, so it is compared with the network's first-user revenue over all 1,946 store orders ($113,924). A check, never added: each answer is one line a buyer picked after checkout, so a gap is a reason to tag links and read the network again, not revenue to count.

blind_spots: Dark social: links shared in DMs and group chats arrive as Direct; the survey is the only check here.
In-app browsers: TikTok's bio link is untagged (7.1% tag coverage), so clicks that lose the referrer in TikTok's browser land in Direct. This account makes this one worse.
View-only influence: people who saw a video and later searched the brand show up as organic search.
Cross-device: a phone visit from Instagram and a laptop purchase are two users to GA4.
Consent and blockers: 21 social-code orders never reached GA4; store orders are the source of truth for the count.
The first-user view over-credits: a purchase driven by an email months later still goes to the network that brought the user first.

utm_convention.rules: lowercase, hyphens not spaces, one tagged bio link per network, no tags on links between the store's own pages

unknowns: X, LinkedIn, Pinterest: the brand doesn't post there, so they are not in the report.
YouTube media value: no YouTube ad spend in the window and no CPM given, so not priced.
changes_made: None. This skill reads and reports only.
